Wagner is played by Sonja Sohn, the same actress who played Detective Kima Greggs in all five seasons of "The Wire."

Although Sohn never won any Emmys for her work on "The Wire" — nor did anyone else on the show , irritated fans are often quick to note — her performance was still praised for how grounded and distinct it felt. She made her mark behind the scenes, too, as the show ended up backing out of its original plan to kill her off near the end of Season 1. In the tenth episode, "The Cost," Greggs was supposed to die in the shootout that occurs, but HBO exec Carolyn Strauss convinced showrunner David Simon to let her survive.

Greggs was also praised for being one of a small number of openly queer female characters on TV at the time. When an interviewer at Curve Magazine asked her in 2020 how she felt about suddenly becoming "a lesbian sex symbol," Sohn replied, "You know, some things you just don't have control over. And it's not that I mind. I was kissing Sam Jackson in 'Shaft ,' and all of a sudden, I became like a serious hottie, you know, among straight black men. It's my job as an actress to inhabit many worlds and to do it convincingly."

entertainment.title: Louis Gossett Jr. Starred In A '80s Sci-Fi Series That Flew Under The Radar
entertainment.summary: Louis Gossett Jr. won an Oscar for one of his 1982 roles, but another project from that year was a sci-fi series that lasted just one season on NBC.
entertainment.body:
That summer, Gossett's film "An Officer and a Gentleman" premiered, earning him an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. In September, he starred in the sci-fi series "The Powers of Matthew Star." The show follows an alien prince (Peter Barton) who is forced to hide out on Earth, disguised as a high school student, after his home planet is invaded. He is accompanied by his guardian (Gossett), who poses as a science teacher.

Created by "Die Hard" screenwriter Steven E. de Souza, "Matthew Star" premiered on NBC and featured some familiar sci-fi talent behind the scenes. " Star Trek " actor Leonard Nimoy directed Episode 9, while his co-star, Walter Koenig, wrote Episode 10.

Before the series premiered, a pyrotechnics accident on set injured Gossett and left Barton with second- and third-degree burns, delaying production for four months. The series ultimately ran for only 22 episodes before NBC pulled the plug in 1983.

NBC Despite its challenging production, "The Powers of Matthew Star" was a welcome opportunity for Louis Gossett Jr. By the 1980s, Gossett wanted the freedom to take on a wide variety of roles without being typecast.

"I am so grateful that the public has given me this gift," Gossett told The New York Times about being appreciated for his talent rather than being defined by his race. "They look at me as a person — not as a race, or a color. The word for it is freedom, to be accepted as — me."

The Emmy winner, who made history as the first Black actor to win an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor, went on to star in other sci-fi projects, including 1985's "Enemy Mine" with Dennis Quaid. At the age of 83, Gossett appeared in HBO's hit superhero series "Watchmen," for which he earned his eighth Emmy nomination. Gossett died five years later in March 2024 at the age of 87.

In a 2025 interview with CinemaBlend , Amirah J, who portrays Morgan's (Kaitlin Olson) daughter Ava, opened up about the specific ways that Olson facilitates the depiction of their characters' relationship. "She asked for my input a lot with different scenes that we'll have," revealed Amirah J. "She's like, 'Would you actually say this? Would a teenage girl actually say this? Can we change it?'"

Much of "High Potential" is driven by the mystery of what happened to Ava's birth father, Roman Sinquerra, who disappeared 15 years before the start of the series. This long-unanswered question forms the complicated center of the relationship between Morgan and Ava — but just as Morgan never stops trying to connect with her daughter, Olson is always keeping up with her young co-star, whether or not the cameras are rolling. "Even when we're not filming, she's very motherly and nurturing, just asking about what's going on in my real life," recounted Amirah J. "When I was doing prom a few months ago, she was like, 'Send me all your prom pictures and all your stuff' ... super mom vibes."

ABC/YouTube When it comes to her portrayal of a single mother on "High Potential," Kaitlin Olson's own kids are never too far from her mind. Speaking to Deadline about her "High Potential" character, Olson said, "I am a mom, I have two kids. It's the most important job I've ever done. So, being able to bring an aspect of that to this character was really special." Despite the wide range of memorable roles on her acting resume — from the outrageous Dee in "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia" to the shameless titular protagonist of "The Mick" — playing a mom on "High Potential" offers her a new opportunity to draw on untapped facets of her personal life.

"High Potential" Season 2 ended on several notable cliffhangers , disclosing new information about the ever-evasive Roman while also foreshadowing danger in Ava's future. With Season 3 of "High Potential" poised for a January 2027 release, fans of the ABC show are closer than ever to reuniting with their favorite fashionable crime-solver.

But no matter what the upcoming episodes of "High Potential" have in store, it seems all but certain that highlighting Morgan's role as a mother will continue to be a series priority. "One of the things I love about this show is the heart and soul of it is Morgan with her family," Olson told Deadline. "We're solving crimes, and that's the basis of the show, but at the heart of it is this woman who is doing this for her kids."

sports.title: Kyle Shanahan: Brock Purdy's ankle sprain is "more mid than low"
sports.summary: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy emerged from Sunday's win over the Vikings with an ankle injury.
sports.body:
“It’s too soon, but I’m pretty optimistic about it,” coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Friday. “But, I was about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it’ll be all right.”

Next Sunday, the 49ers visit the Giants. The following weekend, the Rams visit.

Shanahan also revealed some details about the specific nature of the ankle sprain.

“Anytime it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. “Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. Didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down.”

Purdy’s performance in 2026 has made him one of the favorites to win the NFL MVP award.

sports.title: Mike Macdonald on Sam Darnold, when healthy: "I think he's done a good job"
sports.summary: Quarterback Sam Darnold is back as Seattle's starter this week, after missing two games due to quad and rib injuries.
sports.body:
On Friday, coach Mike Macdonald was asked to assess Darnold’s performance when healthy.

“I think he’s done a good job,” Macdonald said. “As a football team, we’ve been good enough to go 6-4, and we want to get better. Yeah, he’s right there with everybody else.”

Well, he’s not right there with the player who replaced him. Drew Lock has started three games and played all but one drive of another. His record is 4-0. Darnold is 2-4.

And their numbers are starkly different. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. Lock has thrown seven touchdown passes and no interceptions.

Lock’s games have come against the Patriots, the Cardinals twice, and the Raiders. Darnold has faced the Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, and Bears — a much tougher slate of opponents.

The Seahawks won a Super Bowl with Darnold. That counts for something. Still, they’re 6-4. They have an opportunity to get a seventh win on Sunday, with Brock Purdy out for the game against the 49ers.

sports.title: No Aaron Rodgers? No problem. Steelers crush Broncos with dominant defense
sports.summary: Mason Rudolph did enough on a day when the Steelers' defense made life miserable for Bo Nix.
sports.body:
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix could do nothing in Pittsburgh, as the Steelers’ defense dominated in a 27-5 win.

Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph, starting for the first time since Aaron Rodgers was benched and released, played reasonably well, completing 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards, with one touchdown and no interceptions. The Steelers didn’t ask Rudolph to do a lot, but what they asked him to do, he did.

But the Steelers’ defense was outstanding. T.J. Watt recovered a Nix fumble in the end zone for one touchdown, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception for another touchdown, and the Steelers’ defense had a great day on a rainy Black Friday in Pittsburgh.

The win improves the Steelers’ record to 7-4 and erases any doubt that head coach Mike McCarthy can lead them to the playoffs this season. The loss drops the Broncos to 8-3, and raises questions about how far they can go with Nix at quarterback.

sports.title: 49ers announce Mac Jones will start vs. Seahawks, Brock Purdy is out
sports.summary: Purdy's ankle injury will force him to miss his first game of the season.
sports.body:
Brock Purdy, who is an MVP candidate this season, has not practiced all week with an ankle injury, and on Friday, head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that Purdy has been ruled out. Shanahan said Jones is ready to go and will play well on Sunday.

“Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac.”

Last year Jones started eight games while Purdy was hurt, and although Jones didn’t play as well as Purdy, he did play well enough for the 49ers to go 5-3 in those eight games.

Now the 49ers will hope Jones can play well enough to beat the defending Super Bowl champions in a game that has major implications for the NFC playoff race.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers: Sanctity of the locker room doesn't protect the coach from accountability
sports.summary: With Al Michaels calling today's game in Pittsburgh, ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers texted Michaels to give his side of the nasty breakup he just had with the team and head coach Mike McCarthy.
sports.body:
During the fourth quarter of the Broncos-Steelers game, Michaels read a text from Rodgers, in which Rodgers claimed he in no way violated the sanctity of the Steelers’ locker room when he went on Pat McAfee’s show to detail his problems with McCarthy.

“A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers said in the text Michaels read during the game. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.”

Rodgers told McAfee that McCarthy, among other issues, wasn’t watching enough film, was sleeping in team meetings, and addressed the team as the “Packers” instead of the Steelers during halftime on Sunday.

McCarthy’s Steelers are dominating the Broncos today, which stands as a rebuke to Rodgers’ claim that McCarthy isn’t fit to be the team’s coach. But Rodgers was able to get his side of the story into the game, via his text to Michaels.

sports.title: Sam Darnold officially off injury report, set to start vs. 49ers
sports.summary: Sam Darnold is officially back.
sports.body:
As expected, the Seahawks’ quarterback is off the injury report and set to start against the 49ers on Sunday, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Friday afternoon.

Darnold has been listed as a full participant throughout the week after missing Seattle’s last two games with a quad injury. Darnold had also suffered a cracked rib in the Week 8 loss to the Bears.

Darnold has had turnover issues this season, throwing nine interceptions this season. He’s thrown at least one pick in each of his last six starts.

Seattle is 3-4 in games that Darnold has started and 3-0 in games with Lock as QB1. Lock also brought the Seahawks back in the Week 1 win over the Patriots after Darnold exited due to injury.

Additionally, the Seahawks have ruled out right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee), and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe) for Sunday’s game against the 49ers.

sports.title: Luke McCaffrey gives up No. 11 to Brandon Aiyuk
sports.summary: Receiver Brandon Aiyuk is back, and he'll be back in the only number he's ever worn in the NFL.
sports.body:
Via multiple reports, Aiyuk and Commanders receiver Luke McCaffrey have struck a deal to give No. 11 to Aiyuk, who joined the practice squad two days ago.

The move strongly suggests that Aiyuk will be making his debut for the Commanders, sooner rather than later. And, at a more subtle level, that he’s not being viewed by the organization as a guy who’s getting a last chance to show that he still has gas in the tank, but as a player that the Commanders regard as someone who will step in and contribute.

Aiyuk won’t play on Sunday at Arizona. He could be on the field as soon as Week 13, against the Titans.

sports.title: Browns sign LS Rex Sunahara to four-year extension
sports.summary: The Browns have signed a key special teams contributor to a new deal.
sports.body:
Cleveland announced on Friday that the club has signed long snapper Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.

Sunahara grew up in Northeast Ohio in Bay Village, which is around 18 miles from where the Browns play at Huntington Bank Field.

“It’s a dream come true. There’s no place I’d rather be,” Sunahara said, via Kelsey Russo of the team’s website. “There’s no team I’d rather be with, so it’s the best thing ever. It makes you really think about a lot of things, where the sacrifices that were made to help get me here, it makes you feel really good.”

Sunahara has appeared in 39 games for the Browns over the last three seasons, including all 17 last season and all 10 so far in 2026.

He and the rest of the Browns will play the Raiders on Sunday night this weekend.

sports.title: Bo Nix throws directly to Jalen Ramsey for pick-six as Steelers dominate the first half
sports.summary: The Broncos' offense has been awful today.
sports.body:
Nix threw a perfect pass directly to a wide-open Jalen Ramsey for a touchdown, which would be great if Ramsey played for the Broncos, but was not so great because Ramsey plays for the Steelers.

It’s impossible to tell what Nix thought he was doing on the play, but he threw the ball right into Ramsey’s hands, and Ramsey returned the interception 36 yards to the house for a pick-six that gave the Steelers a 24-5 lead.

It was the second Steelers defensive touchdown off a Nix turnover; Nix also dropped the ball in the first quarter and T.J. Watt recovered for a touchdown.

Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph hasn’t been great, but he’s been a lot better than Nix, and the Steelers are rolling over the Broncos in the first half.

sports.title: Brock Bowers questionable for Sunday night vs. Browns
sports.summary: The Raiders may get tight end Brock Bowers back for Sunday's game against the Browns.
sports.body:
Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters in his Friday press conference that Bowers is questionable for the contest.

Bowers is dealing with an ankle injury. While he was listed as limited on Wednesday and Thursday, he did not participate on Friday.

Bowers missed last week’s loss to the Broncos. If he does not play against the Browns, he’ll have some extended time to recover as the Raiders have a Week 13 bye.

The star tight end has 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns in eight games so far this season.

Kubiak also noted that offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson suffered a potentially significant injury during Friday’s practice and has been ruled out.

Defensive tackles Tonka Hemingway, Adam Butler, and Tim Keenan have all been ruled out for Sunday’s game as well.

Defensive tackle JJ Pegues and cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. are questionable.

sports.title: Alex Singleton tackles Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety as Steelers lead 14-5
sports.summary: The Broncos' offense can't do anything, but the defense has done something.
sports.body:
The latest big play on defense came via Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton, who tackled Steelers running back Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety. That made the score 14-2 Steelers. On the subsequent possession, the Broncos kicked a field goal to make it 14-5.

More bad news for the Steelers came when linebacker Jack Sawyer was ruled out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.

Pittsburgh has two touchdowns, one of which came from the defense when T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone. The Steelers’ other touchdown, a Mason Rudolph to DK Metcalf touchdown pass, was the game’s only offensive score.

Rudolph has been better than Nix so far, which few would have expected heading into the game. But this game has been less about the quarterbacks than about the defenses.

sports.title: Dan Quinn had an "absolutely fantastic experience" coaching with Mike McCarthy
sports.summary: With Wednesday's rant from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers painting a negative picture about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy that extended to his time with both the Packers and the Cowboys, those who have worked with him in those places will inevitably be asked about McCarthy.
sports.body:
Commanders coach Dan Quinn, who spent three years as McCarthy’s defensive coordinator in Dallas, got the question on Friday.

“I had a like absolutely fantastic experience coaching with Mike ,” Quinn said, via Ben Standig. “He’s part of the reason I wanted to go there. And over my three years with him, man, I learned a lot. So I can’t speak anything from Pittsburgh but what I can say is like, you know, like I had an unbelievable coaching experience with him. Like, detailed about it. Got me better, challenged me in a lot of ways with how I’m thinking, what it can be, so that would go into it.”

Some will say that Quinn is simply saying all the right things, and that he wouldn’t want to make McCarthy look bad by telling tales of irregularities that may have transpired behind closed doors.

sports.title: Mason Rudolph hits DK Metcalf for touchdown pass as Steelers take 14-0 lead over Broncos
sports.summary: It's been all Steelers in the first quarter in Pittsburgh.
sports.body:
Rudolph threw a well-placed pass toward Metcalf, who leapt into the air over Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain, reeled it in and landed in the end zone for a 22-yard touchdown.

It’s the first start of the season for Rudolph, who has replaced Aaron Rodgers as the Steelers’ quarterback. And it’s the first game for Metcalf since his ejection last week against the Eagles drew him a great deal of criticism — not just for his two personal foul penalties, but for the poor play he has exhibited all season.

There’s still plenty of time left, but in the first quarter, the Steelers look like they’re firing on all cylinders. They’re beating the Broncos 14-0.

sports.title: Tee Higgins did not practice Friday, questionable for Sunday vs. Saints
sports.summary: Bengals receiver Tee Higgins did not practice on Friday, but the injury should not keep him out of Sunday's game against the Saints.
sports.body:
Via Ben Baby of ESPN, head coach Zac Taylor told reporters after Friday’s practice that Higgins woke up with hamstring soreness and the team gave him a day to work through it.

In 10 games this season, Higgins has 867 receiving yards with seven touchdowns. He’s well on pace to set a career high in receiving yards in 2026.

Guard Dalton Risner (knees) is out. Returning from injured reserve, cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) is doubtful while receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is questionable.

sports.title: Joe Milton III praises the Eagles, possibly criticizes the Cowboys
sports.summary: Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III returned to Texas on Thursday and threw a significant wrench into the Cowboys' postseason plans (and, possibly, Philly's thinly-veiled soft tank).
sports.body:
“It was a lot going through my head from when I first got here in Dallas to when I left, all the time I spent doing scout team quarterback, all the times where I was trying to get in the game, when they were up in games, just trying to get more experience,” Milton said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “I mean, it was just great coming back here and playing in this stadium in Jerry’s World and seeing the guys that I worked hard with in fall camp and OTAs.”

He then focused on his current team. While possibly adding a little commentary regarding his former team.

“But I mean, it’s about the Eagles,” Milton said. “These guys show up every day. Nobody’s late to anything. Nobody’s complaining about anything. That’s all you can ask for. That’s the most important thing that I love about this team. I just know they’re going to keep fighting.”

The obvious implication is that, in Dallas, some guys were not showing up every day. Some guys were late. Some guys were complaining.

There are surely complaints today, one day after the Cowboys lost their fourth game of the season while scoring 30 or more points.

sports.title: Steelers score first as T.J. Watt recovers Bo Nix fumble in end zone
sports.summary: There hasn't been any offense on display in Pittsburgh so far on Black Friday, but there has been a touchdown.
sports.body:
On third-and-15 at his own 19-yard line, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix dropped back to pass and was immediately pressured, and he did about the worst thing he could have done: He dropped the football, which rolled into the end zone, where Pittsburgh’s T.J. Watt fell on it for a touchdown.

The player everyone is watching today is Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph, making his first start of the season after Pittsburgh benched and then cut Aaron Rodgers. Rudolph hasn’t done anything of note — he has just five passing yards through two Pittsburgh drives — but he hasn’t made any big mistakes either.

Nix made a very big mistake, Watt capitalized, and that’s the difference in the game so far.

sports.title: Kyler Murray off injury report, likely to be No. 2 QB vs. Falcons
sports.summary: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is officially off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
sports.body:
While he’s not going back to his starting role after Minnesota traded for Kirk Cousins, he probably going to be a snap away.

sports.title: Overturning Rashee Rice fourth-quarter catch to incomplete was correct call
sports.summary: Of course a Buffalo Bills site would run this article with this headline, right? Really though, I wanted to get the bottom of the controversial call that went in the Bills’ favor on the Chiefs second-to-last possession in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s epic 13-10 walk-off win over Kansas City on Th
sports.body: Of course a Buffalo Bills site would run this article with this headline, right? Really though, I wanted to get the bottom of the controversial call that went in the Bills’ favor on the Chiefs second-to-last possession in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s epic 13-10 walk-off win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night. And I’ve reached a very definitive conclusion. The review was correct. Rashee Rice did not catch the football. We have to dismiss the “eye test” here, because NFL’s rulebook is the governing guide to the game. That distinction first has to be established. As convoluted as it may be to some, this is the official rule. It’s a catch if a player: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/catch-rule.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] My good bud Joe Goodberry — a wildly popular and insightful Bengals analyst and Niagara Falls native + resident — explained Friday on Twitter. Here’s the start of his thread, which featured a civil disagreement (yes, they’re possible!) between Joe and Sam Monson of the 33rd Team: [Media: https://twitter.com/JoeGoodberry/status/2126328590811697279?a=Mts4-WLSLMAXwJ951Pc&s=20] Instead of pasting each component of the lengthy back-and-forth between Goodberry and Monson, I’ll summarize the correct interpretation of the rule here. Rice satisfied (a) and (b) on this play. He secured control of the ball first before hitting the ground, then his elbow hit the ground while in control. But, scroll up to check (c) again. Rice did not “perform an act common to the game” — because he was simply falling to the turf, not a common act — therefore he must survive the ground. So, (a), (b), and (c) together were not fulfilled. Had they been, it would have been a catch. Case close. Precisely what occurred on the Rice play is clearly defined in section (2) of the rule. It specifies if (a) and (b) are satisfied, a player does not “survive the ground” if he hits the ground and loses control of the ball, there is no possession if the ball hits the ground before he regains control. That is exactly what happened on the play. Was it an egregious loss of control from Rice? [Media: https://twitter.com/oscolaidhe55/status/2126329351419359373?a=TtIZoWiYSK7VSyxJqic&s=20] No. But any degree of losing control counts if the ball hits the ground in the process. Which is why the NFL got this call right.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers got no support from the Thanksgiving broadcasts
sports.summary: The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him.
sports.body:
Across the board, the reaction from the NFL’s analysts and broadcasters was negative.

Former Steelers quarterback and Fox analyst Terry Bradshaw went off . Fox’s Michael Strahan agreed that Rodgers shouldn’t have gone public with his complaints — calling him a “narcissist” and a “rich jerk” and a “rich bad teammate.”

Fox’s Howie Long said that the moment “defines who [Rodgers] is.”

“He’s a guy that I think picked the wrong sport,” Long said. “He probably should have played tennis.”

Fox’s Rob Gronkowski said that, even if a contender loses its starting quarterback, there’s “too much smoke” to justify bringing Rodgers in.

The CBS pregame crew offered similar views . Nate Burleson said Rodgers “ didn’t handle this right .” Bill Cowher said he hates to see a Hall of Famer go out this way . Russell Wilson said, “It’s about Aaron Rodgers’s legacy. . . . If I’m his family members, if I’m somebody close to him, I’m his significant other, whatever it may be. ‘ Is this how you want to go out? ’ After all the success he’s had, is this how you want to go out? . . . This is a disappointment.”

During the Eagles-Cowboys game, Fox’s Tom Brady criticized Rodgers for violating the “ sanctity ” of the locker room.

The irony, if I’m using the term correctly (I never know), is that Rodgers has previously railed about leaks from the locker room.

sports.title: Broncos, under Bo Nix, are much better at home than on the road
sports.summary: Lost in the ongoing drama in Pittsburgh is that they play the 8-2 Broncos today.
sports.body:

With their 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, the Bills have matched the best 11-game start in franchise history. It was ugly. It was wet. It was cold. It was supposed to be an epic showdown between two NFL MVP quarterbacks. But in the end, it was a 57-yard field goal in the rain that sailed straight and true off the foot of Tyler Bass as the clock expired. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2126171219808354598?a=IFl7N-Ac-9ck3p1FlOA&s=20] In 67 seasons of Bills football, only three other teams have made it through their first 11 games with just one loss. If you’re looking for a little reason to be optimistic about where this season could be headed, let’s take a look at what those three teams went on to accomplish. The 1964 Bills, under head coach Lou Saban, finished their regular season with a 12-2 record before defeating the San Diego Chargers, 20-7, to win the first of back-to-back AFL championships. It would be another 24 years before Buffalo got off to another 10-1 start. In 1988, Marv Levy’s Bills finished the regular season at 12-4, winning the AFC East for the first time since 1980 and making it to the AFC Championship Game, where they lost to the Cincinnati Bengals. Three years later, the Bills were at it again. The 1991 team turned its 10-1 start into a 13-3 regular-season record and made the second of Buffalo’s four consecutive Super Bowl appearances. Now we can add Joe Brady’s 2026 team to that list. Brady has won 10 of his first 11 games as an NFL head coach. sports.summary: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. sports.body: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. After all, if you’ve listened to enough of Allen’s postgame press conferences, you know there’s one statistic he cares about more than any other — wins. With Buffalo’s 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Allen has now won 98 regular-season games, tying Russell Wilson for the most wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons. Wilson, who entered the league in 2012, never had a losing season during his first nine years with the Seattle Seahawks. He won double-digit games in eight of those nine seasons, including a career-high 13 in 2013. Allen, on the other hand, won just five games as a rookie in 2018. A year later, the Bills were back in the playoffs, and they haven’t had a losing season since. In fact, Buffalo extended its franchise record to eight consecutive winning seasons just last week with a win over the Miami Dolphins. Allen moved past Patrick Mahomes (95) on this particular list two weeks ago when the Bills beat the New York Jets. Now, having picked up another win at Mahomes’ expense, Allen has caught Wilson, too. Allen completed just 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards while adding 43 yards on the ground. The real hero of the night was Tyler Bass who scored seven of the team’s 13 points – including the game winning field goal from 57 yards. But football is a team sport, and Allen’s contribution still counts. And the win is his to claim. The Bills will be in New England next week, where Allen will have his first opportunity to take sole possession of the NFL record. Allen still has six regular-season games left in his ninth season. That gives him some time to make life a little more difficult for the next quarterback chasing this record.

If they lose to the Miami Dolphins in Week 12, that’ll reduce their chances to less than 1%. However, if they beat the fish, their playoff chances will double to 2%. Are you saying there’s a chance? There’s a section of the fan base that would prefer to see the Jets lose to both improve their draft positioning and to lessen the chances of Aaron Glenn returning in 2027. The problem, according to some of those fans, is that there are too many winnable games down the stretch for the Jets. On paper, the Jets will be or could be facing at least three backup quarterbacks (Carson Beck or Josh Johnson, Kyle McCord, and Tommy DeVito). Also, depending on whether the Buffalo Bills have anything left to play for in Week 18, that could be a fourth backup QB. Instead of complaining, why don’t we take advantage? This opens up a favorable pathway to go on a winning streak. Now, how likely is that? Well, that’s a different conversation altogether. The Jets haven’t won back-to-back games all season. They haven’t really upset anyone, and they haven’t consistently beaten teams that folks assume they should be able to beat. Both of those things would be necessary to even have a hint of the postseason. The other thing helping the Jets’ potential path is that the bottom of the AFC is falling apart. Pittsburgh is crumbling; the Jets have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland; they play New England; and Baltimore has a backup in at QB. I’m not saying it’s likely; I’m not guaranteeing it’s going to happen; all I’m saying is there’s a chance, and maybe that’s what Jets fans should be rooting for. The Indianapolis Colts are self-destructing. The Jets control their first-round pick. That pick has a great chance to be a top-three selection. The Jets don’t need to tank; the Colts can tank for them. So… playoffs?! Maybe I’m food drunk from Thanksgiving, but I’m starting to see the light! --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: Late in the Buffalo Bills win over the Kansas City Chiefs, a turning point in the game was decided by replay. On third down inside two minutes, Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice over the middle of the field and Rice was popped by Bills safety Amani Hooker. As he fell to the ground, the ball moved. On the field it was ruled a catch. Because it was inside two minutes, the replay official had to call for a review and not Bills head coach Joe Brady. After replay, it was ruled an incomplete pass. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the play, saying he didn’t like the call. “Not one that I agreed with,” said Reid of the replay review. “This came from New York,” Reid said. “They called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. To me that was not clear and obvious.” The NBC broadcast spent a lot of time on it during the game and again in the postgame. Rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it was a catch and the Chiefs should have moved the chains. Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. sports.body: Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau moved into a tie for seventh place on the team’s all-time sacks list on Thanksgiving night. Rousseau sacked quarterback Patrick Mahomes on a 3rd & 16 midway through the third quarter on Thanksgiving night to bring his career total to 43, catching former Bills defensive end Mario Williams. [Media: https://twitter.com/NFL/status/2126156691347808404?a=4Khc_jbNIPbmkep54LM&s=20] Williams spent four seasons (2012-2015) in Buffalo, recording double-digit sacks in each of his first three years with the team. His best season came in 2014 when he recorded 14.5 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Rousseau, now in his sixth NFL season, has spent his entire career in Buffalo after the Bills selected him with the 30th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Having already established a new personal single-season record for sacks this year, the 26 year old is now working his way through some familiar names in Buffalo’s history books. Once Rousseau gets past Mario Williams, there’s another Williams waiting for him. Former defensive tackle Kyle Williams (48.5), who spent all 13 of his NFL seasons in Buffalo, sits sixth on the franchise’s all-time list. With six regular-season games remaining, and the way Rousseau has been getting to opposing quarterbacks lately, we might not have to wait until next season to talk about him catching another Williams.

sports.body: The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their first three years of existence. They were called the Titans at that point. Playing against the future Kansas City Chiefs, Don Maynard caught 10 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown, while Art Powell added 8 catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. November 23, 1961: New York Titans 21 Buffalo Bills 14 Al Dorow threw for 223 yards and a touchdown, and Dick Felt returned an interception 55 yards for a touchdown to provide the Titans with the winning margin at the Polo Grounds. November 22, 1962: New York Titans 46 Denver Broncos 45 A wild game in Denver saw the Titans blow a 24-7 lead and then overcome a 45-32 fourth quarter deficit on Johnny Green’s fourth and fifth touchdown passes of the game, one to Dick Christy and the other to Art Powell. November 23, 1972: Detroit Lions 37 New York Jets 20 Entering the fourth quarter, the Lions led 23-20, but they blew the game open with a field goal and touchdown runs by Greg Landry from 6 yards and Altie Taylor from 38. November 28, 1985: Detroit Lions 31 New York Jets 20 Eric Hipple threw four touchdown passes, three to Leonard Thompson as the Lions jumped out to a 24-3 lead and never looked back. November 22, 2007: Dallas Cowboys 34 New York Jets 3 It was an ugly afternoon in a lost season for the Jets. The Cowboys owned a 21-3 lead at halftime on a Marion Barber touchdown run, a Jason Witten reception from Tony Romo, and a Terrence Newman interception off Kellen Clemens returned for a score. November 25, 2010: New York Jets 26 Cincinnati Bengals 10 In the third meeting between these teams in eleven months, the Jets erased a 10-7 halftime deficit. Brad Smith was the star with a 53 yard touchdown run in the first minute of the second half and an 89 yard kickoff returned for a score in the fourth quarter. November 22, 2012: New England Patriots 49 New York Jets 19 This game is best remembered for the Buttfumble. What people don’t remember was that was part of a 52 second span where New England scored an offensive touchdown, a defensive touchdown, and a special teams touchdown to turn a 7-0 lead into a 28-0 rout.

sports.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
sports.summary: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. sports.body: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary.
